newsitem.title: UK: Syrian Jan crude talks grind on as time runs out.
newsitem.headline: Syrian Jan crude talks grind on as time runs out.

text.p: Monthly price talks for Syrian crude exports in January were making little headway on Monday with buyers still bidding 25 cents below the latest offer from Damascus, oil traders said.
State-owned Sytrol was offering its January Light crude at Dated Brent less 25 cents a barrel having begun talks over a week ago with an opening offer of Brent plus 13 cents.

Term buyers said the revised offer was still far too high, representing only a 20-cent reduction on December levels, when the price of its main competitor, Russian Urals, has fallen by about 50 cents in the same period.
"We talked to them (the Syrians) this morning and they are still considering their next move," said a buyer.
"Most people I talk to are sticking to (Dated Brent) minus 50 or 55 cents," said another regular customer.
Some buyers were considering not lifting cargoes in January unless Sytrol comes down another 25 cents but others could accept Dated Brent less 40 cents, they said.
With the time available for arranging freight for cargoes loading in early January rapidly running out, buyers were hoping for an agreement later Monday while taking precautionary measures.
"As far as I understand, some people have been opening letters of credit with a provisional price," said a trader.
Negotiations for heavy Souedie crude were also at a virtual standstill, with Sytrol asking Dated Brent less $4.60 a barrel and buyers insisting on a discount of $5 to the benchmark grade.
"If they don't come lower we will definitely not take it," said a term buyer.
The value of sour crude in the Mediterranean slid 10 days ago as Iraq began selling its first exports for more than six years under an U.N. oil-for-food deal.
European refiners have signed up for as much as two-thirds of the 500,000 barrels per day (bpd) Baghdad is allowed to sell to raise $2 billion every six months for humanitarian purposes.
